title: NeoVitaDB catalog entry
description: One homebrew entry. Contributors write this file; the build workflow resolves the rest (version, date, size, download count, checksums, download URL) from the GitHub release.

id.description: Stable numeric id, never reused. It is the catalog primary key: the app stores it in the favourites file and uses it to recognise itself. Max 4 digits. Unique only within its own platform - apps/vita/ and apps/psp/ each have their own id space, so a vita entry and a psp entry may share the same id.

name.description: Homebrew name, without version. The app renders 'name version'.

category.description: Maps to the numeric type the app filters on.

titleid.description: Required for vita entries, ignored for psp. Exactly 9 uppercase alphanumerics.

repo.description: GitHub repository holding the releases, as owner/name. Required unless direct_url is set - an entry hosted entirely outside GitHub (its own server, a non-GitHub git forge, ...) has no repo to name, and skipping it also skips the GitHub-specific trust/version-resolution logic that assumes one.

asset.description: Glob matching the release asset to publish. Defaults to *.vpk.

prerelease.description: Set true to track pre-releases too. Nightly builds should stay false, or every build looks like an update. Ignored when direct_url is set - there's no 'latest release' selection to honour it.

direct_url.description: Pins the entry to one specific download URL instead of resolving repo's latest release + asset glob. If it's a https://github.com/{repo}/releases/download/{tag}/{file} URL for this entry's own repo, the build still fetches that tag's release for version/date/changelog/downloads (just pinned instead of latest) - everything works as normal. Otherwise (a raw.githubusercontent.com link, another repo's asset, a non-GitHub host entirely, ...) there's no release to introspect, so 'version' becomes a required, contributor-maintained field instead of build-derived, and date/changelog/downloads fall back to best-effort values. A homebrew with no GitHub repo at all can also just omit 'repo' - 'source' then links to this URL's own host instead of a GitHub page. See README.

version.description: Only meaningful (and required) alongside a direct_url that isn't one of the entry's own repo's release assets - there's no release to read a version from, so the contributor bumps this by hand whenever direct_url is updated. Ignored otherwise (the build always derives version from the resolved release).

icon.description: File name under icons_vita/ or icons_psp/ (matching platform). The app shards storage by the first two characters, so names must be unique within their platform's icon folder and start with two safe characters.

description.description: Shown in the info panel. May contain newlines. Must never contain the two-character sequence quote-comma, which terminates the field in the on-device parser.

requirements.description: Plain text shown before install. No quotes at all: this field is terminated by the first quote.

screenshots.description: Paths relative to the published catalog root, e.g. screenshots/0001-1.png. Joined with ';' and must fit 511 characters in total.

trailer.description: Base name of an mp4 published under videos/ in the catalog.

data.description: Optional full URL of a separate data-files archive (zip or psarc).

ai.description: Flags homebrew built with AI assistance. Surfaced by a dedicated filter and icon.

trusted.description: Whether the repository has more than TRUSTED_STARS GitHub stars. Written by tools/build_catalog.py itself on every run; do not set this by hand, a scheduled build overwrites it.
